issue_context.title: A lot of old, unused and not existent in Fritzbox device trackers are not removable
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have lots of not existant device trackers in my HA. These devices have been deleted in my Fritzbox long time ago.
After the latest Update, all my device tracker have been doubled, so that I detect these very old ones, sometimes with up to 4 copies xx_2, xx_3 and so on.

As it is not possible to delete them, can you provide a way to delete them permanently without having to edit config files in .storage?
If not, I'd like to place a feature request for a function or service, which enables me to delete those entities anyway.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.8.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

??

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Fritz!Box Tools

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

comments:
Hi @Pirol62, thx for the report!

We definitively planned a “clean-up” service, but will investigate to allow deleting individual devices as well.

Will check once back home from vacations.

Simone

Hey there @mammuth, @aarondavidschneider, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`fritz`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L177) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

For me, remove Fritz, restart and add again, solved this problem.
I think many of them are from a time before the last updates.

Removing individual devices is not trivial, will go for a cleanup service ;-)

Simone
I Thought, that entities without relation to other entities, automations, sensors or scripts can be simply deleted, when they are not connected to their service.
